title: The theme song 'You Don't Love Me' and the band's pianists
summary: The theme song written with Cottrell and Lloyd Glenn, retitled True by Paul Gayton, and the pianists Freeman, Glenn and Reason.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Oh, there's something else that I told you I saw, I was talking to Emmanuel Sales the other day.
Yeah. Fine. He said to tell you that he thinks that Cottrell and a couple other guys, a trio recorded a tune that you and Cottrell wrote. And one of the names was True.

Do you remember that? Do you have another name? That was the theme song. The actual title of the song is You Don't Love Me. Now Paul Gayton is the one that changed the name from You Don't Love Me to True.

That was later then. That is correct. Much later. That's when it was first recorded. Paul Gayton is the one that put it on. Then later on I got Camille Howard to play it but she played it in the wrong vein. She played it in the jump tempo and You Don't Love Me isn't a jump song. It was the theme song of the band. Cottrell, myself and Lloyd Glenn. The pianist that was in my band. He came after Freeman didn't he? Long after Freeman. Yes he came quite a while after Freeman. I think that, I'm not for sure I think there was, no he might have been the one after Freeman. Then there was Lionel Reason, that's another pianist that's playing now. And I think that was the three pianists that I had. Freeman, Lloyd Glenn, oh no, Jay Golson. He was the arranger. He's in Detroit now, a tremendous arranger.
